candidates.computation_change_reason: Acute and chronic dissolved chromium III limits are hardness-dependent formulas, not fixed numbers; a different hardness value or formula interpretation yields different enforceable numeric limits for compliance comparison.

Lead acute and chronic limits depend on both hardness and separate correction factors (CF3/CF4); interpreting whether CF3 and CF4 are always applied, or resolving hardness, changes the computed enforceable limit.
Copper acute and chronic aquatic criteria are hardness-adjusted; different hardness inputs or formula readings change which numeric limit applies to reported dissolved copper measurements.

The row shows numeric acute (750) and chronic (87) aquatic criteria alongside 'Need TMDL'; interpreting whether TMDL status makes these limits non-operative, report-only, or still enforceable changes limit applicability (A), whether monitoring for TMDL-related obligations applies (B), and how missing or non-numeric results are classified (C).

The '(P)' designation and paired criteria values '88 and 30' in the Livestock & Wildlife column versus single values in Aquatic columns leave ambiguity about which numeric criterion is the operative enforceable limit for a given use or endpoint.

Multiple paired limit notations ('10 and 200', '340 and 150') across domestic supply, irrigation, and aquatic columns require interpretation of which value governs compliance for a given parameter and protection endpoint.

Copper row lists site-specific ambient/effluent concentrations, derived instream waste concentrations, hardness-based aquatic criteria, and paired domestic/wildlife limits ('1300 and 500', '20.4 and 13.1'); choosing among these columns or paired values changes the applicable enforceable limit.

Chromium (III) dissolved shows 1E+100 in several criteria columns but numeric acute/chronic aquatic values matching the hardness formulas; interpreting 1E+100 as non-operative versus selecting the aquatic criteria column changes whether a numeric compliance limit applies.

Chromium (VI) has fixed acute (16) and chronic (11) aquatic criteria distinct from chromium (III); determining which chromium species a reported 'chromium, dissolved' measurement represents changes the applicable limit.

A separate 'Chromium, dissolved' row lists different numeric criteria (100/100/1000) than the speciated III and VI rows; interpretation of whether total dissolved chromium or speciated limits apply affects limit selection.

candidates.computation_change_reason: Column headers define instream waste concentration as 2.13*Ce and list multiple parallel criteria families; interpreting which column supplies the enforceable effluent or instream limit for a given pollutant changes compliance calculations.

Blank ambient/effluent cells, zero instream waste concentrations, 1E+100 in multiple criteria columns, and a numeric domestic criterion (2000) coexist; interpreting blanks and 1E+100 as no numeric limit versus selecting the domestic criterion affects limit applicability (A) and whether missing results imply no required comparison or unresolved evidence (C).

Nitrite + nitrate has site-specific Ca/Ce and derived instream values but N/A across domestic, irrigation, aquatic, and health columns except irrigation (132); interpreting which, if any, column provides an enforceable limit—or report-only monitoring—affects limit comparison (A), monitoring obligation scope (B), and classification of absent numeric results (C).

Total residual chlorine lists N/A for domestic irrigation criteria but numeric aquatic acute (19), chronic (11), wildlife (11), and human health (4000) values; selecting the operative protection endpoint determines which enforceable numeric limit applies.

The MQL (2.5) appears alongside numeric criteria; interpreting MQL as a reporting/detection threshold versus a compliance floor affects whether sub-MQL or missing results count as adequate evidence of monitoring (B) and how no-result periods are classified (C).
